source: De Sabbata, Sumers, Griffiths (2024) Rational Metareasoning for LLMs - reward and setup
finding: Direct use of value of computation as a training reward. Reward = gain in log-prob of the answer from the chain minus a per-token cost. Trained with Expert Iteration.
numbers: Reward R=U-C; U=log pi(y|z,x)-log pi(y|x); C=0.1*tokens. K=4 chains, temp 0.5, 5 iterations. 1024 train items each from ARC, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, ProofWriter. Models Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B.
limits: Training, not a scaffold. Only verifiable-answer tasks, no tool cost, only Expert Iteration tested.
agent_relevance: The VOC formula is cheap to compute offline. Could define a code-side score for 'did this thinking help' without model judgement.

source: De Sabbata, Sumers, Griffiths (2024) Rational Metareasoning for LLMs - main results
finding: Rational reward gave fewer tokens at equal or better accuracy than STaR and few-shot CoT.
numbers: Avg accuracy 3B: STaR 47.4, RaM 50.1, CoT-few 34.8, Instruct CoT 53.2. 8B: STaR 61.9, RaM 63.5, CoT-few 56.4, Instruct CoT 60.9. Output tokens 3B 222.7 to 170.8 (-23.3%), 8B 215.1 to 146.2 (-32.0%). vs few-shot CoT -34.8% and -42.3%.
quote: RaM achieves better performance while using significantly fewer input and output tokens compared to STaR or CoT Few-Shot.
limits: Paper quotes token savings inconsistently (23-45% abstract, 23-42% contributions). Small models only.
agent_relevance: A saving of a quarter to a third of thinking tokens without accuracy loss is a realistic target for an S0 gate.

source: De Sabbata, Sumers, Griffiths (2024) Rational Metareasoning for LLMs - adaptive compute and OOD
finding: Trained model thinks longer on hard items than easy ones. Out of distribution the saving held but accuracy was mixed.
numbers: 3B: easy 72 tokens vs hard 145. 8B: easy 89 vs hard 139. MMLU-CF: 3B STaR 27.0% (150.6 tok) vs RaM 29.5% (96.3); 8B STaR 40.2% (153.6) vs RaM 36.4% (110.6), -3.8 points.
limits: One OOD set; 8B lost accuracy. Instruct CoT varied only 0.5-0.9% by difficulty.
agent_relevance: Difficulty-sensitive effort is learnable, but a gate must be checked for accuracy loss on new domains (G7).

source: Oh and Gobet (2025) Monitor-Generate-Verify
finding: Conceptual proposal: add a monitoring step before generating, grounded in metacognition and resource-rational ideas (FOK as stopping signal, belief-MDP control, VOC thresholds). No experiments.
numbers: No empirical results. Cites 'about 20% accuracy loss' from a prefix-dominance trap, taken from Luo et al. 2025, not measured here. Satisficing params alpha, gamma, lambda never given values.
limits: Theory only, NeurIPS 2025 workshop paper. Interpretive choices like exponential threshold decay.
agent_relevance: Matches an S0 pre-gate design, but untested; treat as a design sketch, status [D].

source: Callaway, Gul, Krueger, Griffiths, Lieder (2018) Learning to select computations (BMPS)
finding: Older AI system for the same idea. Learns a near-optimal metalevel policy by mixing myopic value of information and value of perfect information with 2-3 weights tuned by Bayesian optimisation.
numbers: Stopping task: BMPS within 5.19% of optimal, no significant gap for cost>0.0025; 6.78-35.8% better than meta-greedy (20.3% mean). Bernoulli tree: BMPS 0.6535 vs optimal 0.6596 (99.1%), meta-greedy 0.60, full deliberation 0.20, DQN 0.58. Mouselab planning: 98.4% of optimal (0.367 vs 0.373).
limits: Needs exact model of own belief state; VPI integration cost grows exponentially with parameters. Simulated tasks.
agent_relevance: A cheap 'stop or keep computing' rule can reach about 98-99% of optimal. A code-side stopping rule is plausible.

source: Callaway et al. (2018) BMPS - tornado evacuation overhead test
finding: Metareasoning pays for its own overhead when object-level computation costs far more than the metareasoning.
numbers: T=24 h, 10 or 30 cities. Metareasoning cost about 1 ms (10 cities), 3 ms (30 cities), at most one simulation. Benefit larger with more cities and peaked at intermediate simulation cost. 5000 rollouts per setting.
limits: Hypothetical scenario. Authors say it works best when the problem repeats, so offline training amortises.
agent_relevance: Direct support for G7: a gate is worth it only if it is cheap relative to thinking.

source: Snell, Lee, Xu, Kumar (2024) Scaling LLM test-time compute optimally
finding: Best way to spend test-time compute depends on question difficulty. Allocating by difficulty beat uniform best-of-N.
numbers: Compute-optimal beat best-of-N with 2-4x (abstract 'more than 4x') less compute. Smaller PaLM 2-S* with test-time compute beat a ~14x larger model on FLOPs-matched easy and medium items. 5 difficulty bins from 2,048 samples each; MATH 12k train/500 test. Naive revision turned about 38% of correct answers wrong. Beam search worsened on easy questions as budget grew.
quote: Test-time and pretraining compute are not 1-to-1 exchangeable.
limits: One model family and MATH. Predicted difficulty costs 2,048 samples, not counted. Hardest bin barely improved.
agent_relevance: This is the resource-rational allocation result: effort by difficulty. S0 should estimate difficulty cheaply and route. Revision without a signal hurts (supports G1, G2).

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: simple test-time scaling
finding: Budget forcing: cap or extend thinking by suppressing or appending 'Wait'. Accuracy scales with thinking up to a plateau.
numbers: s1K: 1,000 items from 59,029. s1-32B AIME24 50.0 no extrapolation, 53.3 with 2x Wait; MATH500 93.0; GPQA 57.6 to 59.6 with Wait. 2x with no string: MATH500 90.2, GPQA 55.1. Plateau near 30k tokens; 12 of 30 AIME24 responses exceeded context in parallel setup.
quote: Suppressing the end-of-thinking token delimiter too often can lead the model into repetitive loops
limits: Forcing more thinking can loop. Gains modest at the top (+3.3 AIME).
agent_relevance: Forced extra thinking gives only a few points and can loop. Supports 'think more only on a signal' (G1).

source: Chen et al. (2024) Do NOT think that much for 2+3=? Overthinking of o1-like LLMs
finding: Reasoning models spend huge compute on trivial questions; most extra rounds add nothing. Self-training cuts tokens while keeping accuracy.
numbers: On '2+3' o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens than conventional models. First solution correct in over 92% of cases. SimPO FCS+Reflection on QwQ-32B: GSM8K 94.8->96.0 acc, 772.8->416.6 tok (-46.1%); MATH500 93.0->92.8, -44.7%; GPQA 59.6->59.1, -35.4%; AIME24 46.7->43.3, -45.6%.
quote: In more than 92% of cases, the initial round of solutions produces the correct answer.
limits: Two o1-like models. AIME24 lost 3.4 points. Intro and table disagree on which set gave -48.6%.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that unconditional thinking is wasteful on easy items. An S0 gate should send easy items to a short path.

source: Chen et al. (2024) overthinking - efficiency metrics
finding: Defines outcome efficiency (tokens to first correct answer over total) and process efficiency (share of tokens in distinct strategies). Later solutions repeat earlier ones.
numbers: Most responses have 2-4 rounds (76-80% QwQ, 59-63% R1). Avg solutions: QwQ 3.5 ASDIV/3.2 MATH500; R1 4.5/4.3. Solution 4+ distinctness 11.5% lower than solution 3.
limits: Metrics rely on a model-labelled notion of distinct strategy.
agent_relevance: A code-side check of 'is this new round different from the last' could be the stopping signal.

source: Aggarwal and Welleck (2025) L1: controlling how long a reasoning model thinks
finding: Train model (LCPO, RL) to obey a token budget given in the prompt. Accuracy trades off smoothly with budget.
numbers: 1.5B base (DeepScaleR). Targets 512-3600 tokens. Length error about 3% on math, 20-40% out of domain. Vs S1 at 512/1024 tokens: +20-25 points absolute. Log-linear slope 0.24 vs 0.37. At matched short length about +5% over Qwen-2.5-1.5B-Instruct and +2% over GPT-4o. L1-Max avg soft violation 1.3%, hard about 9%.
quote: L1's length control allows for smoothly trading off computational cost and accuracy on a wide range of tasks
limits: Needs training. May not generalise to lengths beyond those trained. Additive reward variant collapsed to very short chains.
agent_relevance: Budget-conditioned thinking exists; a scaffold can set the budget from the S0 gate and the model respects it roughly.

source: Han et al. (2024) Token-budget-aware LLM reasoning (TALE)
finding: A prompt alone, with a zero-shot budget estimate, cuts output length a lot at small accuracy cost. Too small a budget backfires (token elasticity).
numbers: GPT-4o-mini over six math sets: tokens 461.25->148.72 (about -68%), accuracy 83.75->81.03. Cost 289.78->118.46. GSM8K up 81.35->84.46. Across 4 models on MathBench-College: -64.63% tokens, worst drop GPT-4o-mini 78->70. Budget 50 gave 86 tokens, budget 10 gave 157 tokens (vs 258 vanilla). Llama-3.1-8B TALE-PT-SFT GSM8K 77.56->78.57 acc, 241.5->139.6 tok.
quote: the token cost increases, indicating that further reductions in the budget lead to increasing token consumption
limits: Math only. Accuracy fell on some models.
agent_relevance: Prompt-level budget is a no-training lever. Do not set absurdly low budgets: the model overshoots.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) AdaptThink
finding: Model learns to choose Thinking or NoThinking per question. A learned S0 gate.
numbers: R1-Distill-1.5B: length -53.0%, accuracy +2.4 on average. 7B: -40.1%, +2.3. 1.5B NoThinking picked on 86.9% of GSM8K, 76.8% of MATH500, 40.4% of AIME24. GSM8K 79.0/978 tok -> 83.1/480; MATH500 80.6/4887 -> 82.0/1782; AIME24 29.4/12073 -> 31.0/6679. NoThinking alone: GSM8K 69.8, MATH500 67.2, AIME24 14.0.
quote: AdaptThink reduces the average response length of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B by 53% and improves its accuracy by 2.4%.
limits: Trained on 40K math items; distilled R1 models only.
agent_relevance: Closest published match to an S0 gate. Skipping thinking on easy items costs nothing and can help. Gate chose no-think for most easy items.

source: DEER (2025) Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models
finding: Training-free stop rule: at thought transitions, probe a trial answer and stop if the model is confident.
numbers: 11 reasoning models 1.5B-671B, 10 benchmarks. CoT length -19.1% to -42.9% (main models) up to -80.1%; accuracy +0.3 to +5.0. Latency -27.9% to -40.1%.
quote: reducing the length of CoT sequences by an average of 19.1% to 80.1% while improving accuracy by 0.3% to 5.0%
limits: Confidence comes from the model itself; calibration failures can cut real reasoning.
agent_relevance: A stopping rule that runs on a probe outside the reasoning is cheap. Confidence is model-judged, so pair with a check.

source: Does thinking more always help? Mirage of test-time scaling in reasoning models (2025)
finding: Longer thinking helps then hurts. Early gains tied to higher output entropy, not better reasoning. Splitting the same budget over parallel paths with a vote beat longer chains.
numbers: R1-Distill-1.5B GSM8K 82.2->87.3% at 385->1,100 tokens, down to 70.3% at about 15,980 tokens. MATH500 83.2->78.3% with extended thinking; entropy 0.12->3.0. Parallel thinking about 22% above Wait & Think More at 16K budget (abstract: up to 20%).
quote: Our study is limited to mid-sized models due to resource constraints
limits: Mid-size models only (1.5B-8B). Variance account uses a simple Gaussian model.
agent_relevance: There is an optimal stopping point per item. More thinking is not free. Voting from one model is not independent (G4), so test on checks.

source: Hassid et al. (2025) Don't overthink it: preferring shorter thinking chains
finding: Among sampled chains for one question, shorter ones are more often correct.
numbers: Shortest chain up to 34.5% more accurate than longest for the same question; +2.2 to +15.7 points over random pick on math. short-1@k matches majority voting with up to 40% fewer thinking tokens; short-3@k beats it and is up to 33% faster. Finetune S1-short +2.8% relative, 5.8% fewer tokens.
quote: longer thinking does not necessarily translate to improved performance
limits: Models LN-Super-49B, R1-32B, QwQ-32B, R1-670B; competition math and GPQA.
agent_relevance: Chain length is a free signal in code (G5). A length-based selector among attempts costs nothing.

source: Aggarwal, Madaan, Yang, Mausam (2023) Adaptive-Consistency
finding: Sequential Bayesian stopping rule for self-consistency: stop sampling once the leading answer is stable.
numbers: 17 datasets, 3 models (GPT-3.5-turbo, Vicuna-13B, code-davinci-002). Beta criterion, threshold 0.95. About 3.3x fewer samples (Table 5: 3.2x), up to 7.9x on Boolean Expressions; mean accuracy drop 0.07 points.
quote: Adaptive-Consistency reduces sample budget by up to 7.9 times with an average accuracy drop of less than 0.1%.
limits: Agreement among samples of one model is not independent evidence (G4).
agent_relevance: A code-run stopping rule on answer counts is a cheap VOC proxy. Use it to stop sampling, not to assert truth.

source: Li et al. (2024) Escape sky-high cost: Early-stopping self-consistency (ESC)
finding: Sample in small windows; stop when a window is unanimous.
numbers: Mean sample reduction: MATH -33.8%, GSM8K -80.1%, StrategyQA -76.8%, CommonsenseQA -78.5%, Coin Flip -84.2%, Last Letters -67.4%. Accuracy change vs SC about 0 for GPT-4; GPT-3.5 StrategyQA -0.19, Llama-2-7b StrategyQA -0.14, Coin Flip -0.14 (units as printed in the paper's table). Window 5 (8 for MATH), max 64/40 samples.
limits: Weaker models lose accuracy on some sets.
agent_relevance: Cheap early exit works best for strong models and easy items.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time compute
finding: Do thinking offline before the query arrives; it shifts compute cost off the live path.
numbers: Same accuracy with about 5x less test-time compute on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME. Scaling sleep-time gave up to +13% and +18%. With 10 queries per context cost per query down up to 2.5x. SWE-Features 33 PRs: about 1.5x fewer tokens at low budgets; at high budgets standard test-time won.
limits: Helps only if queries are predictable from context. Five parallel generations beat 10.
agent_relevance: Resource-rational trade across time: amortise thinking over repeated queries about one context. Relevant to a long-lived agent.

source: Chain of Draft (2025)
finding: Terse intermediate steps instead of long CoT.
numbers: Abstract: uses as little as 7.6% of the tokens of CoT and matches or surpasses CoT in accuracy. No other figures read.
limits: Only the abstract page was read; tasks and models not checked.
agent_relevance: A cheap prompt-only compression lever, to be tested at equal tokens.

source: Stop overthinking: survey of efficient reasoning (2025)
finding: Taxonomy of efficient reasoning: model-based (RL length reward, SFT on variable length), output-based (latent, dynamic inference), prompt-based (budget, routing by difficulty).
numbers: Cited figures: 4,018 agentic trajectories, picking lower overthinking scores gave +30% performance and -43% compute. 'Which is bigger, 0.9 or 0.11' took 19 s on QwQ-32B, 42 s on R1.
limits: Survey; secondary numbers not re-verified.
agent_relevance: Map of methods; routing by difficulty is the S0 family.

source: Liu, Geng, Peterson, Sucholutsky, Griffiths (2024) LLMs assume people are more rational than we really are
finding: LLMs predict human choices as closer to expected value than humans are. Resource-rational noise in humans is not modelled by them.
numbers: choices13k, 9,831 problems. Human corr with max-EV 0.48. GPT-4o CoT corr with EV 0.94 (GPT-4-Turbo CoT 0.93, Llama-3-8B CoT 0.57, GPT-4o zero-shot 0.28). Corr with human choices about 0.60-0.62 for best models.
quote: LLMs assume that people are more rational than we really are
limits: Not a test of resource-rational analysis itself; uses the term only to explain the gap.
agent_relevance: Models solve for the full-computation answer. They do not simulate cost-limited thinking unless forced, so cost-awareness must come from the scaffold.

source: Binz and Schulz (2023) Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
finding: GPT-3 matched or beat humans on some decision tasks but showed no directed exploration and failed causal reasoning.
numbers: 12 vignettes: 6 right. CRT 3 items: intuitive wrong answer all 3. Horizon bandit: short horizon no difference t(5566)=-0.043; long horizon lower initial regret t(5550)=-4.07, final regret n.s.; mean regret 2.72 vs human 3.24. No horizon effect on directed exploration beta=-0.15, p=.58. Only davinci beat chance on about 13,000 problems.
quote: GPT-3 failed spectacularly in using an underlying causal structure for its inference
limits: Old model (text-davinci); not about computation cost.
agent_relevance: Baseline showing the model lacks explore-exploit logic of its own; gate rules belong in code.

source: Chen et al. (2025) O1-Pruner length-harmonizing fine-tuning
finding: RL fine-tune with a length reward shortens long-thought models and keeps accuracy.
quote: relatively high accuracy is preserved even within shorter-length intervals
limits: Two models, math only, single run with no variance, authors' own AES metric. Training on easy items shortened output without gain.
agent_relevance: Another independent case of shorter thinking at equal accuracy; savings of one third are typical.

source: Wang et al. (2025) MRT: optimizing test-time compute via meta reinforcement fine-tuning
finding: Reward progress (change in estimated chance of success) per episode on top of outcome reward; framed as minimising cumulative regret over thinking.
numbers: Gain over base 2-3x that of GRPO; 1.5x token efficiency over GRPO, 5x over base; backtracking setting 1.6-1.7x. Avg pass@1: DeepScaleR-1.5B base 54.5, GRPO 55.0, MRT 55.9; R1-Distill-1.5B 44.9, 46.0, 47.1.
quote: leads to a 2-3x relative gain in performance
limits: Absolute gains are about 1-2 points. 20 samples per problem.
agent_relevance: Progress-per-step is the operational form of value of computation. A progress monitor could trigger S0 changes (see Progress monitoring).

source: Lieder and Griffiths (2020) Resource-rational analysis (BBS)
finding: Founding paper: derive models of cognition by asking for the best use of limited computation. Not read this session (publisher page timed out); listed from prior knowledge only.
numbers: No numbers read this session.
limits: Not opened; do not cite figures from this line.
agent_relevance: Basis for the S0 gate idea: compare expected gain of more computation to its cost.

source: Oh and Gobet (2025) sec. 7.2 on strategy selection as a contextual bandit (after Lieder and Griffiths 2017)
finding: Describes strategy selection as a contextual bandit with Thompson sampling over strategy weights and a VOC formula (their Eqs. 47-53).
numbers: Equations only, no data. Parameters not assigned values.
limits: Secondary description; the 2017/2018 originals were not opened.
agent_relevance: A code-side bandit over reasoning modes is the standard resource-rational recipe.
